schema_note: No contracts/*.md or scripts/tickets_shapes.py schema currently names a canonical findings-record shape (contracts/result.md's `--findings-file` mechanism and CritiqueAdjudication carrier are retired per its and work-item.md's T0 supersession records; contracts/dispatch.md line 99, ahead of its first T0 record, confirms the live mechanism is a plain `findings: <path>` line the frame journal relays verbatim). The seven fields below (id, seam, blocking, summary, evidence, cause, remedy) are this judge's own choice, made in that gap, and are offered as successor material for whoever next canonicalizes a findings shape.

findings.summary: templates/host-block.md's shipped routes text (399/400 words) cuts the design's 'name the lane in one line before working' sentence and two of its three tripwires (second concern mid-act -> brick; scope splitting -> frame), keeping only the unknown-cause tripwire. This is law cut for budget, not connective prose trimmed: it removes two of the design's three named, behavior-changing escalation rules and the UX contract's stated always-say-it-first requirement from the one place the host block's own vocabulary entry calls normative, and no test in the repository asserts any of the three tripwire sentences or the say-the-lane sentence, so nothing caught it across 13 lands.
findings.evidence: templates/host-block.md line 10 ('Route by need, smallest first. **act**' -- no 'name the lane' clause) and lines 25-26 ('Tripwires promote, never predict: an unknown cause investigates before any edit.' -- only one of three); research/routing-design-2026-08-31.md lines 110-119 (### Tripwires, three bullets) and lines 172-179 (## The UX contract: say the lane out loud) and lines 206-230 (the design's own drafted-verbatim block, which contains all three tripwires and the say-the-lane clause); tests/test_thin_orchestrator.py test_outline_route_consumes_the_root_shape_it_sealed (asserts only 'an unresolved goal' / 'one planning orch-do' / 'the planner never drives', never the tripwire text) and a repo-wide grep for 'name the lane', 'second concern', 'splitting scope', 'tripwire' under tests/ returning zero hits; B1.md frame journal 'land-B1.4-arm' record ('B1.4's trims ... flagged for the seam judge').
findings.cause: The host block's routing-law sentences (tripwires, UX contract) have no demand-anchor test, so a budget-constrained trim silently dropped behavioral law instead of only the already-legitimate connective compression the same commit also did elsewhere in the same paragraph (comparing the design draft's 231-word routes text to the shipped 189-word routes text: ~18 of the ~42 cut words are the tripwires/say-the-lane content itself; the remaining ~24 are genuine compression such as dropping 'narrowly', 'in the medium's own history it makes itself', 'durable', 'adding nothing').
findings.remedy: Minimal re-trim inside the same 400-word ceiling (verified via tools.validate_support.packages.body_words, the validator's own counting method): restore 'name the lane in one line before working' (+8 words) and the two missing tripwire clauses, e.g. 'a second concern mid-act enters brick, scope splitting enters frame,' (+10 words); offset by cutting the sentence '`evolve` and `benchmaker` run only when named.' (-7 words), which only restates the untouched preamble's already-general 'named items still run only when named' for two named examples, and by cutting 'prints the freed frontier' (-4 words), a descriptive detail on land's output with no rule or test attached to it. Net after those four moves is +7 words (399 -> 406); a similarly-sized further compression (e.g. tightening 'each wave re-read its `## Report`;' or a comparable connective phrase already in the same family B1.4 trimmed) closes the last ~6 words. This is a proposal for the driver's one repair round, not applied here (judge tickets read and grep only, per this ticket's Details). Successor: add a demand-anchor test pinning the three tripwire clauses and the say-the-lane sentence the way test_outline_route_consumes_the_root_shape_it_sealed pins the outline clause, so a future budget trim cannot repeat this silently.

findings.summary: B1.2's CELL_DUPLICATION_ALLOWLIST 'verification-scope anchor' family is scoped to exactly the mandated sentences: no more, no fewer. Clean verification, no defect.
findings.evidence: tools/validate_support/duplication.py lines 44-66 list exactly six clauses: the five pack-specific 'Run the narrow affected X' sentences plus the one shared closing clause 'the full suite is the gate's row, never a unit's'. A live grep of all five packs' references/craft.md ('Run the narrow affected' / "gate's row") in packs/orch-code-pack, orch-content-pack, orch-data-pack, orch-design-pack, orch-research-pack shows each pack carries exactly one of the five variants plus the shared clause, verbatim, matching the allowlist one-to-one with none left over and none of the five packs missing. scripts/tickets_assignment.py line 54 (CRAFT_SCOPE_ANCHOR = "gate's row") is a live reader of this exact sentence, confirming the mandate is functionally load-bearing (this judge's own dispatch prompt was constructed by that reader from orch-code-pack's craft.md). git log confirms 2eb006de ('B1.2: plant the verification-scope anchor in the four remaining packs') is the commit that added the family.

findings.summary: B1.5's decision to keep `tickets.py new`'s flag form while B1.1/B1.12 deleted the review_kind apparatus under the same 'test-only reachability is not liveness' standard is a principled, evidenced distinction, not an inconsistency: `new` is a live, directly-typeable, documented CLI verb (it stays in tickets_commands.py's SUBCOMMAND_USAGE/SUBCOMMAND_SUMMARY tables) that shares real production machinery (pinned_pack_digest) with the live `do`/brick-minting door, whereas the deleted review_kind lane required hand-fabricating a gate-stage ticket id shape that no live door -- not even a human typing an ordinary command -- could ever produce. `new` is not documented anywhere as more than a fixture factory in current prose docs, but its own --help summary text gives no hint that it is retained specifically as a test-fixture factory rather than a recommended authoring path.
findings.evidence: scripts/tickets_issue.py line 86 (_cmd_new) is called only from scripts/tickets_dispatch.py line 150 ('if command == new: return _cmd_new(rest)'), i.e. only via the documented CLI verb -- no internal caller. scripts/tickets_issue.py's pinned_pack_digest (line 52) is also called from scripts/tickets_brick.py line 224, the live `do`/`judge` brick-minting path, confirming test_new_pins_the_stamped_packs_digest_at_issue_time (tests/test_tickets.py, PackPinTest, run live: 5/5 pass) exercises shared machinery through `new`'s door rather than testing something unique to `new`. Commit 003c16e3 ('Retire new --file...') states directly: 'its flag form -- minting a ticket from --executor/--goal/--context -- is kept: it is the standing test fixture for the dispatch/staleness/semantic-contract/done-predicate suites, so it has a surviving lawful caller and the subcommand is not deleted whole.' A repo-wide grep of README.md, DESIGN.md, TICKETS.md, docs/*.md, rules/*.md for 'tickets.py new' returns zero hits; README.md line 251 teaches `do --goal-file` as the one hand-authoring door. contracts/work-item.md line 381 ('tickets.py new and lint grade a ticket's shape, never its length') is an incidental historical mention, not a recommendation. scripts/tickets_commands.py line 73: SUBCOMMAND_SUMMARY['new'] = 'Create one Goal/Context ticket; Details is the planner's optional free-form guidance.' -- phrased identically in register to 'do' and 'judge''s summaries, with no fixture-only caveat.
findings.cause: The fixture-maker role is recorded only in the frame journal (B1.md, private ticket history) and the commit message, neither of which a future reader consulting `tickets.py --help` or `tickets.py new --help` would see.
findings.remedy: Successor scope (not a blocker): a one-line addition to SUBCOMMAND_SUMMARY['new'] or NEW_USAGE noting it is retained as the test-fixture door for surviving machinery, so a future author does not reach for it as a second hand-authoring path alongside `do --goal-file`.

findings.summary: contracts/work-item.md, contracts/dispatch.md, contracts/result.md and scripts/tickets_shapes.py agree with each other and with the code at this tip across all three deletion waves (review_kind at B1.7, checker apparatus at B1.12, new --file at B1.5): every mention of a retired term (review_kind, review_v1, checked_by, review_stage, GatePlan/CritiqueAdjudication/RepairOutcome, --findings-file/--accepted-file/--artifact) sits inside a 'T0 supersession record' block, which test_ticket_protocol.py's own normative-prose check partitions out before asserting absence -- confirmed these are historical, not live, claims. tools/regen.py --check (run live) returns {"failed": {}, "skipped": {}, "stale": {}}, confirming tickets_shapes.py is current against the code that generates it. One shape-fidelity gap found and reported here: the `independence` frontmatter field (kept by all three deletion waves) is now fully inert -- not merely its 'checker' enum value as B1.12's own findings flagged, but the whole field -- because scripts/tickets_brick.py and scripts/tickets_frame.py hardcode BRICK_INDEPENDENCE = "gate" on every live door, and the field's only other read site (scripts/tickets_issue.py line 194) is lint's own enum-membership check, never a behavioral branch.
findings.evidence: tests/test_ticket_protocol.py lines 84-92 (normative = dispatch.partition('T0 supersession record')[0]; assertNotIn on each retired term against `normative` only) run live and green. contracts/work-item.md lines 430-452 and contracts/dispatch.md lines 135-152 and contracts/result.md lines 108-124 place every retired-term mention inside a 'T0 supersession record sha256:...' paragraph; contracts/dispatch.md line 99 (before its first T0 record at line 162) states the live mechanism instead: 'a review lane is told to print `findings: <path>` as a second verbatim line' -- matching this ticket's own dispatch instructions. `tools/regen.py --check --json` run from the workspace root returned exit 0 with an empty failed/skipped/stale report. grep of scripts/*.py for 'independence' (excluding tests) shows every non-test site is a write of a hardcoded 'gate' (tickets_brick.py:231, tickets_frame.py:105, tickets_done.py:162/325 via BRICK_INDEPENDENCE="gate" at tickets_brick.py:81) or a shape/enum declaration (tickets_generations.py:21, tickets_shapes.py:120, tickets_issue.py's INDEPENDENCE_VALUES/'_issue_defects' at lines 43/194-196); no site anywhere branches behavior on the field's value. B1.md 'land-B1.12' record already flags 'inert independence:checker enum value' as successor-queue material.
findings.cause: The independence field predates the routing design's judge-as-brick model; once every live door was hardcoded to 'gate' and the checker-stage machinery it distinguished against was deleted, the field's only remaining job is being written and syntax-checked, never decided.
findings.remedy: Successor scope, already queued by B1.12 (this finding only sharpens its boundary from 'the checker value is inert' to 'the whole field is currently decorative'): fold the constant literal into ticket issuance directly, or restore a real reader for the value, in the successor's own pass -- not this judge's edit.

findings.summary: The run's demand-anchor moves are not vacuous at the merged tip. All three of B1.13's stated acceptance greps were re-run live and hold exactly: host-block route lane markers are exactly {act, brick, frame, outline} (no answer/single/graph/fix survive as route names); 'review_kind' has zero occurrences under scripts/ and contracts/; no tickets_review* module file exists. The two named demand-anchor test suites (TestHostBlockBrickFlags in tests/test_installer_cases/managed_text/host_block.py via tests/test_installer_managed.py, and tests/test_thin_orchestrator.py's frame/outline route-slice tests) were run live and all pass (63 and 15 tests respectively, 0 failures), and each anchor string they assert was independently confirmed to appear exactly once, inside the correctly-bounded slice of templates/host-block.md, so these are real passes rather than string-coincidence. The one coverage gap this sweep surfaces is the explanatory cause behind F1: the demand-anchor test family protects flag lists, lane names, and per-lane step sequences, but asserts nothing about the tripwire or say-the-lane sentences, which is how F1's cut crossed 13 lands undetected.
findings.evidence: Live command output: grep -oE for '**act**|**brick**|**frame**|**outline**|**answer**|**single**|**graph**|**fix**' against templates/host-block.md returned exactly act/brick/frame/outline; grep -rc review_kind scripts/ contracts/ returned no nonzero lines; find scripts -iname 'tickets_review*' returned nothing. `python -m unittest tests.test_ticket_protocol tests.test_thin_orchestrator -v`: Ran 15 tests, OK. `python -m unittest tests.test_installer_managed -v`: Ran 63 tests, OK. tests/test_thin_orchestrator.py lines 203-219 (test_outline_route_consumes_the_root_shape_it_sealed, slices strictly between the unique markers '**outline**' and '`install.py doctor`') and lines 102-134 (test_frame_lane_emits_the_wave_lifecycle, slices between '**frame**' and '**outline**') were read in full and their asserted anchors matched the shipped host-block.md text read directly.
findings.cause: n/a -- see F1's cause; this finding documents the re-verification, not a new defect.
findings.remedy: n/a beyond F1's remedy, whose successor item (a tripwire/say-the-lane demand-anchor test) also closes this coverage gap.
